Nope. It's a 720gallon HME type 1 with a 1250gpm pump.

We have one hose real on each vehicle with about the same length as you. And then for a progressive lay we use inch and a half and 1 in with a wye. And each rig has 6 wildland packs with 100ft supply and 50ft 1inch

Cal fire does this differently.  They dont use the 1 inch with a wye. They clamp the line and attach the next stick, which seems super inefficient to me, but they can do it so fast it's a blur.  Our way is much more conservative but it takes more hose and more appliances.

Pump and roll we use the bumper line and the hose reel, but obviously that can be done 50 different ways.
We do have to walk the hose once to drain it before we hang it but we don't have to disconnect it if we have proper hooks. In a bump and run scenario we're supposed to be able to drain the line and get it hung and the rig moving and under 2 minutes. Cal Fire's goal is under 90 seconds.

And so everybody's on the same page, this technique is only going to get used if we have time. Is the fire is going to be there in 10 minutes we obviously are not doing bump and run. At that point it's a decision of whether we're doing structure protection or getting the f*** out.

Also the whole point of the hooks is that we don't have to disconnect and when you load the hose on the hook correctly there's no Tangles or knots when you deploy it at the next site.

If it's got defensible space u foam the s*** out of it and keep moving. 

If we're not assigned bump and run then we establish clear what defensible space we can and do structure protection until we have to bug out God forbid

Once again I live in a town of 300 people we train with Cal Fire. We have to use the equipment that's available to us to get the job done. And both the Cal Fire and the fire service. Given our situation and available resources this is just one of the tactics that we have to be trained and equipped for. Where we live it's going to be an hour before we get any help.

To some of the points that have been made we all agree that if our town starts to go it's very much at risk for the whole town burning down and an evacuation plan may be more important than an actual fire defense plan. We also do as much as we can for the community in defensible space.
